questions.q:
For a postmortem report, a doctor requires to know approximately the time of death of the deceased. He records the first temperature at $10 \cdot 00am$~to be $93 \cdot 4 ° F$. After $2$ hours he finds the temperature to be $91 \cdot 4 ° F$. If the room temperature (which is constant) is $72 ° F$~estimate the time of death. (Assume normal temperature of a human body to be $98 \cdot 6 ° F$ )
\left[\log_{\mathrm{e}}\dfrac{19 \cdot 4}{21 \cdot 4} = - 0 \cdot 0426 \times 2 \cdot 303\rightand \left\log_{\mathrm{e}}\dfrac{26 \cdot 6}{21 \cdot 4} =0 \cdot0945 \times2 \cdot303\right]$
questions.solution:
Let $T$ be the temperature of the body at any time $t$.

By Newton's law of cooling $\dfrac{dT}{dt} ∝ \left(T - 72\right)$

since,~$S = 72 ° F$

\dfrac{dT}{dt} =$k \left(T - 72\right)$

$⇒ ∫ dT\left(T - 72\right) = ∫ kdt$

$⇒ ln\left(T - 72\right) = kt + c$

or $T = 72 + ce^{kt}$

At~$t = 0, T = 93 \cdot4 ⇒ c = 21 \cdot4$

[First recorded time $10am$~is $t = 0$]

$∴ T = 72 + 21 \cdot4e^{kt}$

When $t = 120, T = 91 \cdot4$

$⇒ e^{120k} = \dfrac{19 \cdot 4}{21 \cdot 4}⇒ k = \dfrac{1}{120}\log_{\mathrm{e}} \left(\dfrac{19 \cdot 4}{21 \cdot 4}\right)$

$= \dfrac{1}{120} \left(- 0 \cdot 0426 \times 2 \cdot 303\right)$

Let ${t}_{1}$ be the clasped time after the death.

When $t = {t}_{1}; T = 98 \cdot 6 ⇒ 98 \cdot 6 = 72 + 21 \cdot 4e^{la}$

$⇒ {t}_{1} = \dfrac{1}{k}\log_{\mathrm{e}}\left(\dfrac{26 \cdot 6}{21 \cdot 4}\right) = \dfrac{- 120 \times 0 \cdot 0945 \times 2 \cdot 303}{0 \cdot 0426 \times 2 \cdot 303} = - 266min$

[For better approximation the hours converted into minutes]

i.e., $4$ hours $26$ minutes before the first recorded temperature. The approximate time of death is $10 \cdot 00hrs$. $- 4$ hours $26$ minutes.

$∴$~Approximate time of death is $5 \cdot 34am$.&

questions.solution:
$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{2x - 4y - 5}{x - 2y + 2}$

$= \dfrac{2\left(x - 2y + 2\right) - 9}{x - 2y + 2}$

Let~$x - 2y + 2 = t ⇒ 1 - 2\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{dt}{dx}$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{dt}{dx}$

i.e.~$\dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{dt}{dx} = \dfrac{2t - 9}{t}$

$⇒ \dfrac{dt}{dx} = - 2\left(\dfrac{2t - 9}{t} - \dfrac{1}{2}\right) = \dfrac{18 - 4t}{t} + 1$

$⇒ \dfrac{dt}{dx} = \dfrac{18 - 3t}{t} ⇒ \dfrac{t}{18 - 3t}dt = dx$

$⇒ - \dfrac{6 - t - 6}{6 - t}dt = 3dx$

$⇒ - dt + \dfrac{6}{6 - t}dt = 3dx$

Integrating, we get

$- t - 6ln\left|6 - t\right| = 3x + C$

$- x + 2y - 2 - 6ln\left|6 - x + 2y - 2\right| = 3x + C$

$- 4x + 2y - 2 - 6ln\left|4 - x + 2y\right| = C$

$2x - y + 3ln\left|x - 2y - 4\right| = k$

Hence,~$c = 3$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} + cosec^{2} ( x ) \cdot y = cosec^{2} ( x ) \cdot cotx . . . . . . . . . . ( 1 )$

Now, put~$cotx = t$~in RHS

$- cosec^{2}xdx = dtcosec^{2}x = - dty \cdot e^{- cotx} = ∫ e^{- t} \cdot t ( - dt ) = - ∫ t \cdot e^{- t}dt = - [ t ∫ e^{- t}dt - ∫ \dfrac{d}{dt}t ( ∫ e^{- t}dt ) ] = - [ - te^{- t} - ∫ - e^{- t}dt ] = - [ - te^{- t} - e^{- t} ] + C = te^{- t} + e^{- t} + C = e^{- t} ( 1 + t ) + C = e^{- cotx} ( 1 + cotx ) + C .$

options: None of these
questions.solution:
Given,

& & & $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{\left(x - 1\right)2 + \left(y - 2\right)2tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{y - 2}{x - 1}\right)}{\left(xy - 2x - y + 2\right)tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{y - 2}{x - 1}\right)}$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{\left(x - 1\right)2 + \left(y - 2\right)2tan^{- 1}\left(\left(y - 2\right)x - 1\right)}{\left(x\left(y - 2\right) - \left(y - 2\right)\right)tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{y - 2}{x - 1}\right)}$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{\left(x - 1\right)2 + \left(y - 2\right)2tan^{- 1}\left(\left(y - 2\right)x - 1\right)}{\left(x - 1\right)\left(y - 2\right)tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{y - 2}{x - 1}\right)}$

Let,

~ ~ ~$m = x - 1 \text{ and } n = y - 2$

$⇒ dm = dx \text{ and } dn = dy$

$⇒ \dfrac{dn}{dm} = \dfrac{m^{2} + n^{2}tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{n}{m}\right)}{mntan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{n}{m}\right)}$

$⇒ \dfrac{dn}{dm} = \dfrac{1 + \left(\dfrac{n}{m}\right)2tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{n}{m}\right)}{\dfrac{n}{m}tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{n}{m}\right)}$.

Let,

~ ~ ~$n = vm$

$⇒ \dfrac{dn}{dm} = v + m\dfrac{dv}{dm}$

$⇒ v + m\dfrac{dv}{dm} = \dfrac{1 + v^{2}tan^{- 1}v}{vtan^{- 1}v}$

$⇒ m\dfrac{dv}{dm} = \dfrac{1 + v^{2}tan^{- 1}v}{vtan^{- 1}v} - v$

$⇒ m\dfrac{dv}{dm} = \dfrac{1 + v^{2}tan^{- 1}v - v^{2}tan^{- 1}v}{vtan^{- 1}v}$

$⇒ m\dfrac{dv}{dm} = \dfrac{1}{vtan^{- 1}v}$

$⇒ ∫ vtan^{- 1}vdv = ∫ \dfrac{dm}{m}$

Integrating~by parts, we get,

~ ~ & $tan^{- 1}v \cdot \dfrac{v2}{2} - ∫ \dfrac{1}{1 + v^{2}} \cdot \dfrac{v2}{2}dv = lnm + c$

$⇒ \dfrac{v2}{2}tan^{- 1}v - \dfrac{1}{2} ∫ \dfrac{v^{2} + 1}{1 + v^{2}}dv + \dfrac{1}{2} ∫ \dfrac{1}{1 + v^{2}}dv = lnm + c$

$⇒ \dfrac{v2}{2}tan^{- 1}v - \dfrac{1}{2}v + \dfrac{1}{2}tan^{- 1}v = lnm + c$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{n2}{m2}tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{n}{m}\right) - \dfrac{n}{2m} + \dfrac{1}{2}tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{n}{m}\right) = lnm + c$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{y - 2}{x - 1}\right)2tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{y - 2}{x - 1}\right) - \dfrac{y - 2}{2\left(x - 1\right)} + \dfrac{1}{2}tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{y - 2}{x - 1}\right) = ln\left(x - 1\right) + c$

Multiplying both sides by~$2\left(x - 1\right){}^{2}$, we get,

\left(y - 2\right)2tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{y - 2}{x - 1}\right) - \left(y - 2\right)\left(x - 1\right) + ( x - 1{)}^{2}tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{y - 2}{x - 1}\right) = 2 ( x - 1{)}^{2}ln\left(x - 1\right) + c$

$⇒ \left(\left(y - 2\right)2 + \left(x - 1\right)2\right)tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{y - 2}{x - 1}\right) - \left(y - 2\right)\left(x - 1\right) = 2\left(x - 1\right)2ln\left(x - 1\right) + c$.

(i), we get $(7 u-3 v) d u+(3 u-7 v) d v=0\ldots(\mathrm{ii})$ This homogeneous equation in $u$ and $v$. Put, $u=t v \Rightarrow d u=t d v+v d t$ in Eq. (ii), we get $(7 t v-3 v)(t d v+v d t)+(3 t v-7 v) d v=0(7 t-3)(t d v+v d t)+(3 t-7) d v=0\Rightarrow \quad\left(7 t^2-7\right) d v+v(7 t-3) d t=0\Rightarrow \quad \int \frac{d v}{v}+\int \frac{7 t-3}{7 t^2-7} d t=0\Rightarrow \log |v|+\int \frac{t-3 / 7}{t^2-1} d t=C_1\Rightarrow \log |v|+\left[\int \frac{2}{7(t-1)} d t+\int \frac{5 / 7}{(t+1)} d t\right]=\log C_1\Rightarrow \log |v|+\frac{2}{7} \log |t-1|+\frac{5}{7} \log |t+1|=\log C_1\Rightarrow \log |v|+\frac{2}{7} \log \left|\frac{u}{v}-1\right|+\frac{5}{7} \log \left|\frac{u}{v}+1\right|=\log C_1\Rightarrow \log |v|+\frac{2}{7} \log \left(\frac{u-v}{v}\right)+\frac{5}{7} \log \left(\frac{u+v}{v}\right)=\log C_1\Rightarrow \log |v|+\log \left(\frac{u-v}{v}\right)^{2 / 7}+\log \left(\frac{u+v}{v}\right)^{5 / 7}=\log C_1\Rightarrow \log \left[|v| \cdot \frac{(u-v)^{2 / 7}}{(v)^{2 / 7}} \cdot \frac{(u+v)^{5 / 7}}{(v)^{5 / 7}}\right]=\log C_1\Rightarrow \quad \log \left[(u-v)^{2 / 7}(u+v)^{5 / 7}\right]=\log C_1\Rightarrow \log \left[(x-y-1)^{2 / 7}(x+y-1)^{5 / 7}\right]=\log C_1\Rightarrow \quad(x-y-1)^{2 / 7}(x+y-1)^{5 / 7}=C_1\Rightarrow \quad(x-y-1)^2(x+y-1)^5=C$

questions.q: The solution of the initial value problem $\text{(2ln}\text{x}\text{)}\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \dfrac{y}{x} = \dfrac{1}{y}cosx, y > 0, x > 1$~and $\text{y}\left(\dfrac{3\pi}{2}\right) = 0$& is given by which of the following options?
questions.solution:
Given differential equation is

$\text{2}\text{y}\dfrac{dy}{dx} + y^{2}\left(\dfrac{1}{xln x}\right) = \dfrac{cos x}{ln x}$

$⇒ \dfrac{dz}{dx} + \dfrac{z}{xln x} = \dfrac{cos x}{ln x}$

On substituting $y^{2} = z$ and $2\text{y}\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{dz}{dx}$,~we get

$⇒ \dfrac{dz}{dx} + \dfrac{z}{xln x} = \dfrac{cos x}{ln x}$

Which is a $LDE$,

$∴ y^{2}ln x = zln x = sin x + C$

Now,~ $\text{y}\left(\dfrac{3\pi}{2}\right) = 0 ⇒ \text{C} = 1$

$∴ \text{y} = \pm \sqrt{\dfrac{1 + \text\sin\text{x}}{\text\ln\text{x}}}$

~ ~$y = \sqrt{\dfrac{1 + \text\sin\text{x}}{\text\ln\text{x}}} \left(∵ \text{y}> 0\right)$

Required solution~$y = $a\sqrt{\dfrac{1 + sinx}{lnx}}~where $a is any constant.

$

questions.q: The solution of differential equation $\dfrac{dt}{dx} = \dfrac{t\left(\dfrac{d}{dx} ( g\left(x\right) )\right) - t^{2}}{g ( x )}$ is:
questions.solution:
$\dfrac{dt}{dx} - t\dfrac{g^{′} ( x )}{g ( x )} = - \dfrac{t2}{g ( x )}$

$⇒ - \dfrac{1}{t2}\dfrac{dt}{dx} + \dfrac{1}{t}\dfrac{g^{′} ( x )}{g ( x )} = \dfrac{1}{g\left(x\right)}$ ....(i)

Let $z = \dfrac{1}{t} ⇒ - \dfrac{1}{t2}\dfrac{dt}{dx} = \dfrac{dz}{dx}$

$∴$ From equation (i),

$\dfrac{dz}{dx} + \dfrac{g^{′} ( x )}{g ( x )}z = \dfrac{1}{g\left(x\right)}$

On comparing with $\dfrac{dz}{dx} + Pz = Q$, we get,

$P = \dfrac{g^{′} ( x )}{g ( x )}, Q = \dfrac{1}{g\left(x\right)}$

$∴ IF = e^{∫ \dfrac{g^{′} ( x )}{g ( x )}dx}$

$= e^{log ⁡ [ g\left(x\right) ]} = g ( x )$

Thus, the complete solution is,

$z ⋅ g\left(x\right) = ∫ g\left(x\right) ⋅ \dfrac{1}{g\left(x\right)}dx + c$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{t}g\left(x\right) = x + c ⇒ \dfrac{g\left(x\right)}{x + c} = t$

questions.q: The solution of the differential equation \left(1 - x^{2}\right) ⋅ \dfrac{dy}{dx} + xy =  \left(x - x^{3}\$right)y\dfrac{1}{2},\left($∀ \left|x\right| < 1\right)$ is \sqrt{9y} = --$f\left($x\right) + $c\left($1 - x^{2}\right)\dfrac{1}{4},$where $c$ is an arbitrary constant and $f  \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = \dfrac{3}{4} .$Then, $f \left(x\right)$ is$
questions.solution:
Given equation is $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{y}}\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \dfrac{x}{1 - x^{2}}\sqrt{y} = x$
Let $2\sqrt{y} = ν$
$⇒ \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{y}}\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{dν}{dx}$
Thus, we have $\dfrac{dν}{dx} + \dfrac{x}{2\left(1 - x^{2}\right)} ⋅ ν = x$
$∴ I . F . = e^{∫ \dfrac{x}{2\left(1 - x^{2}\right)}dx}$
$= e^{- \dfrac{1}{4}ln ⁡ \left(1 - x^{2}\right)}$
$= {\left(1 - x^{2}\right)}^{- \dfrac{1}{4}}$
Thus, the solution is $ν{\left(1 - x^{2}\right)}^{- \dfrac{1}{4}} = ∫ x{\left(1 - x^{2}\right)}^{- \dfrac{1}{4}}dx$
or $ν ⋅ \left(1 - x^{2}\right)- \dfrac{1}{4} = - \dfrac{2}{3}\left(1 - x^{2}\right)\dfrac{3}{4} + c^{"}$
or $2\sqrt{y} = - \dfrac{2}{3}\left(1 - x^{2}\right) + c^{"}\left(1 - x^{2}\right)\dfrac{1}{4}$
$⇒ \sqrt{y} = - \left(1 - x^{2}\right)3 + c^{'} \left($1 - x^{2}\$right)\dfrac{1}{4}

$⇒ $\sqrt{9y} = - \left($1 - x^{2}\right) + c \left($1 - x^{2}\$right)\dfrac{1}{4}
$⇒ f\left(x\right) = 1 - x^{2}$
$∴ f\left(x\right) is an even function

questions.q: To reduce the differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + P\left(x\right) . y = Q\left(x\right) . y^{n}$ to the linear form, the substitution is:
questions.solution:
The given differential equation is
$\dfrac{dy}{dx} + P\left(x\right)y = Q\left(x\right) . y^{n}$
$⇒\dfrac{1}{yn} . \dfrac{dy}{dx} + y^{- n + 1}P\left(x\right) = Q ( x )$
Put $\dfrac{1}{yn - 1} = v$
~$⇒ \left(- n + 1\right) . y^{- n} . \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{dv}{dx}⇒ \dfrac{1}{( - n + 1 )} . \dfrac{dv}{dx} + P\left(x\right) . v = Q ( x )$
$⇒\dfrac{dv}{dx} + \left(1 - n\right)P\left(x\right)v = \left(1 - n\right)Q ( x )$
Hence, required substitution is $v = \dfrac{1}{y^{n - 1}}$.

questions.q: The curve passing through $P \left({\pi}^{2}, \pi\right) is such that for a tangent drawn to it at a point $Q,$ the ratio of the $y$-intercept and the ordinate of $Q$ is $1: 2 .$ Then, the equation of the curve is$
questions.solution:
General equation of the tangent at $Q \left(x, y\right)$ is $Y - y = m \left(X - x\right)$
Its $y$-intercept $= y - mx$
$∴ \dfrac{y - mx}{y} = \dfrac{1}{2}$
$⇒ 2y - 2mx = y$
$⇒ 2mx = y$
$⇒ m = \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{y}{2x}$
or $∫ \dfrac{dy}{y} =∫ \dfrac{dx}{2x}$
$∴ ln ⁡ y = \dfrac{1}{2}ln ⁡ x + ln ⁡ C$
or $y = C\sqrt{x}$
As it passes through \left({π}^{2}, \pi\right)$⇒ C = 1$
$∴$ The curve is $y = \sqrt{x}$

questions.q: The orthogonal trajectory of& $y^{2} = 4ax$~(where~$a$& being parameter) is
questions.solution:
$y^{2} = 4ax$

$⇒ 2y\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 4a$

So, the differential equation of~$y^{2} = 4ax$~is~$y^{2} = \left(2y\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)x$

$⇒ y = 2x\dfrac{dy}{dx}$

Replace~$\dfrac{dy}{dx}$~by~$\dfrac{- dx}{dy}$~in above equation, we get,~

$y = - 2x\dfrac{dx}{dy}$

$⇒ ydy = - 2xdx$

$⇒ ∫ ydy = - 2 ∫ xdx$

$⇒ \dfrac{y2}{2} = - x^{2} + c$

$⇒ y^{2} = - 2x^{2} + 2c$

$⇒ 2x^{2} + y^{2} = k$& is the required orthogonal trajectory.

$⇒ \dfrac{sin ⁡ y}{x} = \left(\dfrac{- 1}{2}\right)e\dfrac{1}{x2} + C$
